docs.purpose: A panel shown once, right after a user saves their first job, asking whether they would like alerts when their saved jobs change. Saying yes then triggers the phone's own permission prompt; saying 'maybe later' dismisses it without asking the operating system anything. Both choices are given the same visual weight so neither feels like the forced option.
docs.data_story: This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device. It holds no client-side store, so there is no local copy of server state to keep in sync. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the GATE renderer (a `statuses_handled[]` that must cover every value of the closed set it gates on), reading no contract. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/shared/NotificationPermissionModal.tsx`.

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: Three props, one in-repo consumer (SaveButton); a change is one commit.

inputs.why: visible/onAllow/onDismiss only — the MMKV once-per-device gate that decides whether it appears lives in pushTokens, not here.

outputs.why: Allow fires the parent callback, which requests the OS permission and — if granted — registers the Expo push token; the modal itself only closes.
outputs.rollback: none — a denied OS permission is terminal for this prompt; the settings screen is the documented re-request path.

state.why: Its once-per-device contract is an MMKV flag (hasAskedPermission / markAskedPermission) written by SaveButton before the modal opens, so a dismissal is permanent for this entry point.

staleness.why: It renders fixed copy; the OS permission status it precedes is read by the settings screen, not here.

session.why: It can only appear after a save, which requires a session; the registration route is under the authenticated /api/notifications prefix.

rls_class.why: Its downstream write lands on device_tokens — Class A, select/insert/update policies keyed on auth.uid() because the register route upserts.

guards.rate_bucket: none — /api/notifications/register calls no withRateLimit; the ON CONFLICT upsert makes repeat registration idempotent

checks.why: markAskedPermission is written BEFORE the modal opens, so the double-permission pre-prompt fires at most once per install even if the user force-quits mid-prompt.
Both paths carry equal visual weight (bordered containers) so the double-permission pattern offers a genuine choice rather than a dark pattern; the file says so at :12-13.
Both actions carry a role, a label and an explicit minHeight 44.

errors.why: No failure path is rendered: a denied OS permission simply closes the sheet, and a failed token registration is swallowed upstream.

emits.why: Neither Allow nor Maybe Later is instrumented, so the opt-in rate of the double-permission pattern is unmeasurable.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: The surface consumes no registered logic variable: the only server-side tunable in this path, user_profiles.radius_cap_km, is a per-user admin column, not a logic_variables row.

sharing.why: POST /api/notifications/register is reached from here via SaveButton and independently from the root shell on the auth→app transition.

limitations.what: The MMKV flag is written before the OS prompt, so a user who force-quits between the two never sees the pre-prompt again from this entry point.
limitations.measured: SaveButton.tsx:59-62 calls markAskedPermission() then setShowPermModal(true); the settings re-prompt row (settings.tsx:130-177) is the documented recovery.

notes: This overlay is mounted by SaveButton, which is itself unowned under R-13 (rendered by both LeadCard and the lead-detail CTA) — so the chain from a first save to a push registration passes through a component no surface claims.

programme.why: Notifications: one device-token registry and one preference set across both products.
